preset_description: Tailor-made notched sound therapy: broadband pink noise with a band of energy removed around your tinnitus pitch. The idea is that neurons at the notch edges inhibit the over-active tinnitus-frequency neurons, lowering perceived loudness over weeks of daily listening. Based on Okamoto et al. (2010, PNAS), where notched music with a 1-octave notch lowered tinnitus loudness and auditory-cortex activity. The notch width defaults to 0.5 octave, the protocol used by Stein et al. (2016); a study comparing 1, 1/2 and 1/4 octave notches found that width made no difference (Wunderlich et al. 2015). IMPORTANT: the 6000 Hz center here is only an EXAMPLE - you MUST adapt it to your own tinnitus pitch. Press [t] to play a matching tone, tune it until it matches your tinnitus, then press Enter to center the notch there. Best evidence is for TONAL tinnitus at or below ~8 kHz. Use headphones at a comfortable, low level, daily over weeks to months. Evidence is mixed: Stein's 100-patient trial found no effect on its main outcomes, and meta-analyses disagree (Tavanai et al. 2024: no significant effect; Jiang et al. 2025: small benefit). This is an adjunct, not a cure. Not medical advice; consult an audiologist.
